policy.scope: Permanent product terminology and compatibility governance. This slice adds checks and does not rename live modules, packages, hosts, persisted keys, or historical content.
policy.deprecatedAliasMatching: Case-insensitive exact phrase matching for configured aliases; user-facing source literals are scanned, while code/path compatibility remains explicitly allowlisted.
policy.allowlistRule: Every compatibility exception is path-scoped, term-scoped, owned, justified, evidenced, and expires at a named removal gate. Wildcards are intentionally narrow.
policy.historyRule: Immutable history is readable but never rewritten for naming. New source files cannot inherit a history exception unless they match an explicitly immutable historical path.

sourceAuthority.projectionRule: TearBench may project production owners, but must not repeat their IDs, display names, homes, publication state, or mechanic identities in a second catalog.
sourceAuthority.specializedMechanicsRule: Only mechanics named by a canonical environment scenario may receive a specialized terminology projection; generic gameplay terminology is not inferred from this registry.

persistenceImpact.scope: audio vendor paths, cue/catalog formats, replay metadata, provenance, package/scripts, bundle-budget keys
persistenceImpact.canonicalWrite: TEAR Music / tear-music naming for canonical vendor artifacts; retain old paths for compatibility reads

terms.owner: Audio platform/vendor provenance owner with replay-envelope and audio-catalog owners
terms.compatibilityStrategy: Dual-read old audio metadata, cue/catalog formats, vendor paths, package aliases, and imported artifacts; canonical-write new names while preserving provenance and unknown fields.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Remove legacy aliases only after the shipped canonical vendor provenance, redirects, provenance URLs, package aliases, vendoring scripts, the Soundtrack Desk target, old replay/save readers, and imported-artifact reads pass the music migration gate.

terms.owner: Audio composition/music-director owner with replay metadata owner
terms.compatibilityStrategy: Rename only audio-specific product vocabulary; retain generic runtime infrastructure and legacy synth fallback as implementation details.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Retire audio-specific legacy runtime aliases only after the shipped canonical artifact, paired Tone host/license, adaptive tier/session behavior, fallback, metadata, and replay round-trip gates pass; generic runtime names remain unchanged.

persistenceImpact.scope: settings tab, station/catalog formats, audio routing and now-playing snapshots
persistenceImpact.canonicalWrite: music settings route and Music catalog vocabulary

terms.owner: Music-surface/catalog owner with settings navigation and presentation owners
terms.compatibilityStrategy: Accept old signal tab/deep links and catalog format while emitting Music labels/routes and preserving station/cue identity.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Remove signal aliases after settings navigation, catalog dual-read, now-playing snapshots, accessibility labels, and old bookmarks pass the release-window gate.

persistenceImpact.scope: private soundtrack host, admin configuration, access/session policy, storage/filesystem, and cross-repository release metadata
persistenceImpact.canonicalWrite: Soundtrack Desk host, configuration, route, and package vocabulary

terms.owner: Music/Soundtrack Desk owner with required game-integration and infrastructure reviewers
terms.compatibilityStrategy: Dual-read legacy Foundry Studio host, configuration, package, and route aliases; canonical-write Soundtrack Desk only after cross-repository host, access, storage, and release evidence is signed.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Remove Foundry Studio and foundry-studio aliases only after the canonical Soundtrack Desk host, access policy, storage/filesystem, redirects, package/route aliases, game integration, and infrastructure evidence are signed by the Music/Soundtrack Desk owner with the required game and infrastructure reviewers.

persistenceImpact.scope: Replay screen copy and replay.editor action ids only; the cut list is built in memory and never saved
persistenceImpact.canonicalWrite: REPLAY EDITOR panel of the Theater
preserve: replay.editor.toggle, replay.editor.appendClip and replay.editor.media action ids

terms.compatibilityStrategy: None needed: no code reads or writes the old name. Ghost Studio stays a deprecated alias so it cannot return in player-facing copy.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Remove the alias once no player-facing copy or current evidence names Ghost Studio.

persistenceImpact.scope: TearBench scenarios, codecs, evidence routes, workflows and preservation corpus

terms.compatibilityStrategy: No rename in this program; Scenario Console is a facade over existing TearBench State Setup hosts.

removalCheckpoint.condition: Never remove or rename TearBench as part of terminology normalization.

persistenceImpact.scope: Playground menu tab copy and prompt-vocabulary action id only; no saved data

persistenceImpact.scope: Player-facing name of the practice mode opened after the Tutorial, and its tab names; no saved data
